arxiv-2304-01720.title: Higher-order Bragg gaps in the electronic band structure of bilayer graphene renormalized by recursive supermoiré potential
arxiv-2304-01720.creator: Mohit Kumar Jat 1 † , Priya Tiwari 2 † , Robin Bajaj 1 † , Ishita Shitut 1 , Shinjan Mandal 1 , Kenji Watanabe 3 , Takashi Taniguchi 4 , H. R. Krishnamurthy 1, Manish Jain 1, Aveek Bid 1
arxiv-2304-01720.description: Abstract This letter presents our findings on the recursive band gap engineering of chiral fermions in bilayer graphene doubly aligned with hBN. By utilizing two interfering moiré potentials, we generate a supermoiré pattern which renormalizes the electronic bands of the pristine bilayer graphene, resulting in higher-order fractal gaps even at very low energies.

arxiv-2307-12918.title: Power sector benefits of flexible heat pumps
arxiv-2307-12918.creator: Alexander Roth, Carlos Gaete-Morales, Dana Kirchem, Wolf-Peter Schill
arxiv-2307-12918.description: Abstract Heat pumps play a major role in decreasing fossil fuel use in heating. They increase electricity demand, but could also foster the system integration of variable renewable energy sources. We analyze three scenarios for expanding decentralized heat pumps in Germany by 2030, focusing on the role of buffer heat storage.

arxiv-2410-06655.title: Ring-exchange physics in a chain of three-level ions
arxiv-2410-06655.creator: Sourav Biswas, E. Rico, Tobias Grass
arxiv-2410-06655.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sourav Biswas, E. Rico, Tobias Grass. In the presence of ring exchange interactions, bosons in a ladder-like lattice may form the bosonic analogon of a correlated metal, known as the d-wave Bose liquid (DBL). In this Letter, we show that a chain of trapped ions with three internal levels can be used to mimic a ladder-like system constrained to a maximum occupation of one boson per rung.

arxiv-2505-02902.title: Local vs. nonlocal entanglement in top-quark pairs at the LHC
arxiv-2505-02902.creator: M. Fabbrichesi a ​ {}^{a\,\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-1937-3854}{\lx@orcidlogo}}, R. Floreanini a {}^{a}\,\lx@orcidlink{0000-0002-0424-2707}{\lx@orcidlogo}, L. Marzola c , d ​ {}^{{c,d\,\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-2045-1100}{\lx@orcidlogo}}}
arxiv-2505-02902.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. Fabbrichesi a ​ {}^{a\,\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-1937-3854}{\lx@orcidlogo}}, R. Floreanini a {}^{a}\,\lx@orcidlink{0000-0002-0424-2707}{\lx@orcidlogo}, L. Marzola c , d ​ {}^{{c,d\,\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-2045-1100}{\lx@orcidlogo}}}. We show that the entanglement observed in top-antitop quark spin states at the LHC is local in the energy region close to the production threshold. In contrast, nonlocal entanglement is observed in the central boosted region defined by a top-quark pair invariant mass m t ​ t ¯ > 800 m_{t\bar{t}}>800 GeV and scattering angles Θ \Theta satisfying | cos ⁡ Θ | < 0.2 |\cos\Theta|<0.2 .

arxiv-2508-13080.title: Molecular Hydrogen in High-redshift Damped Lyman- α \alpha Absorbers
arxiv-2508-13080.creator: Alon Gurman, Amiel Sternberg, Shmuel Bialy, Rachel K. Cochrane, Jonathan Stern
arxiv-2508-13080.description: Abstract Simulations predict that circumgalactic hydrogen gas surrounding massive ( M halo z = 1 = 10 12 − 10 13 ​ M ⊙ M_{\rm{halo}}^{z=1}=10^{12}-10^{13}\ M_{\odot} ) galaxies at z ∼ 4 z\sim 4 may be predominantly neutral, and could produce damped Ly α \alpha absorbers (DLAs) along sight-lines to background quasars ( Stern et al. 2021 ) .

arxiv-2510-00326.title: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Orchestration: A Foundation Model for Multi-Agent Language Model Coordination
arxiv-2510-00326.creator: Hassen Dhrif
arxiv-2510-00326.description: Abstract The emergence of large language models has enabled sophisticated multi-agent systems, yet coordinating their reasoning capabilities through effective prompt engineering remains a fundamental challenge. We present a theoretically-grounded framework for dynamic prompt orchestration that enhances reasoning capabilities across multiple specialized agents.

arxiv-2510-08797.title: TAPAS: Datasets for Learning the Learning with Errors Problem
arxiv-2510-08797.creator: Eshika SaxenaFAIR at MetaAlberto AlfaranoFAIR at Meta, François ChartonFAIR at Meta, Emily WengerDuke University, Kristin LauterFAIR at Meta
arxiv-2510-08797.description: Abstract AI-powered attacks on Learning with Errors (LWE)—an important hard math problem in post-quantum cryptography—rival or outperform “classical” attacks on LWE under certain parameter settings. Despite the promise of this approach, a dearth of accessible data limits AI practitioners’ ability to study and improve these attacks.

arxiv-2511-07043.title: A catalog of new blue stragglers in open clusters with Gaia DR3
arxiv-2511-07043.creator: Songmei Qin, Jing Zhong, Friedrich Anders, Lola Balaguer-Núñez, Chunyan Li, Yueyue Jiang, Guimei Liu， Tong Tang， Li Chen
arxiv-2511-07043.description: Abstract The high-precision Gaia data release 3 (DR3) enables the discovery of numerous open clusters in the Milky Way, providing an excellent opportunity to search for blue straggler stars in open clusters and investigate their formation and evolution in these environments.

arxiv-2512-00386.title: Convergence of Reflected Langevin Diffusion for Constrained Sampling
arxiv-2512-00386.creator: Tarika Mane
arxiv-2512-00386.description: Abstract . We examine the Langevin diffusion confined to a closed, convex domain D ⊂ ℝ d D\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} , represented as a reflected stochastic differential equation. We introduce a sequence of penalized stochastic differential equations and prove that their invariant measures converge, in Wasserstein–2 distance and with explicit polynomial rate, to the invariant measure of the reflected Langevin diffusion.

arxiv-2602-22140.title: Lumosaic: Hyperspectral Video via Active Illumination and Coded-Exposure Pixels
arxiv-2602-22140.creator: Dhruv Verma, Andrew Qiu, Roberto Rangel, Ayandev Barman, Hao Yang, Chenjia Hu, Fengqi Zhang, Roman Genov, David B. Lindell, Kiriakos N. Kutulakos, Alex Mariakakis
arxiv-2602-22140.description: Abstract We present Lumosaic, a compact active hyperspectral video system designed for real-time capture of dynamic scenes. Our approach combines a narrowband LED array with a coded-exposure-pixel (CEP) camera capable of high-speed, per-pixel exposure control, enabling joint encoding of scene information across space, time, and wavelength within each video frame.

pmc-10698477.title: Mitonuclear interactions modulate nutritional preference
pmc-10698477.creator: M Florencia Camus, Sahutchai Inwongwan
pmc-10698477.description: In nature, organisms are faced with constant nutritional options which fuel key life-history traits. Studies have shown that species can actively make nutritional decisions based on internal and external cues. Metabolism itself is underpinned by complex genomic interactions involving components from both nuclear and mitochondrial genomes. Products from these two genomes must coordinate how nutrients are extracted, used and recycled.

pmc-10731585.title: Codon optimization regulates IgG3 and IgM expression and glycosylation in N. benthamiana
pmc-10731585.creator: Lin Sun, Somanath Kallolimath, Roman Palt, Florian Eminger, Richard Strasser, Herta Steinkellner
pmc-10731585.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Plants are being increasingly recognized for the production of complex human proteins, including monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). Various methods have been applied to boost recombinant expression, with DNA codon usage being an important approach. Here, we transiently expressed three complex human mAbs in Nicotiana benthamiana, namely one IgG3 and two IgM directed against SARS-CoV-2 as codon optimized(CO) and non-codon optimized (NCO) variants.

pmc-11380665.title: Anticipated variability increases generalization of predictive learning
pmc-11380665.creator: Hadar Ram, Guy Grinfeld, Nira Liberman
pmc-11380665.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We show that learners generalized more broadly around the learned stimulus when they expected more variability between the learning set and the generalization set, as well as within the generalization set. Experiments 1 and 3 used a predictive learning task and demonstrated border perceptual generalization both when expected variability was manipulated explicitly via instructions (Experiment 1), and implicitly by increasing temporal distance to the anticipated application of learning (Experiment 3).

pmc-11432236.title: Impact of Newly Diagnosed Left Bundle Branch Block on Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with STEMI
pmc-11432236.creator: Larisa Anghel, Cristian Stătescu, Radu Andy Sascău, Bogdan-Sorin Tudurachi, Andreea Tudurachi, Laura-Cătălina Benchea, Cristina Prisacariu, Rodica Radu
pmc-11432236.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: This study assessed the long-term prognostic implications of newly developed left bundle branch block (LBBB) in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and a single coronary lesion, following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: Among 3526 patients admitted with acute myocardial infarction between January 2011 and December 2013, 42 were identified with STEMI, a single coronary lesion, and newly diagnosed LBBB. A control group of 42 randomly selected STEMI patients without LBBB was also included.

pmc-11639082.title: A missense variant effect map for the human tumor-suppressor protein CHK2
pmc-11639082.creator: Marinella Gebbia, Daniel Zimmerman, Rosanna Jiang, Maria Nguyen, Jochen Weile, Roujia Li, Michelle Gavac, Nishka Kishore, Song Sun, Rick A. Boonen, Rayna Hamilton, Jennifer N. Dines, Alexander Wahl, Jason Reuter, Britt Johnson, Douglas M. Fowler, Fergus J. Couch, Haico van Attikum, Frederick P. Roth
pmc-11639082.description: SummaryThe tumor suppressor CHEK2 encodes the serine/threonine protein kinase CHK2 which, upon DNA damage, is important for pausing the cell cycle, initiating DNA repair, and inducing apoptosis. CHK2 phosphorylation of the tumor suppressor BRCA1 is also important for mitotic spindle assembly and chromosomal stability.

We previously reported neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses 21 days after a single booster dose of trivalent XBB.1.5 (Tri‑XBB.1.5), bivalent Omicron XBB (Bi‑Omi‑XBB), or tetravalent XBB.1 (Tetra‑XBB.

pmc-12533482.title: Enhancing Electronic Availability of Hospital Records Following Interhospital Transfer From Emergency Departments to a Veterans Affairs Hospital
pmc-12533482.creator: James O Jordano, Maureen Fausone, Michael R Cauley, Melissa Rubenstein, Terra Swanson, Kelly Sopko, Michael J Ward
pmc-12533482.description: IntroductionWith regionalization of specialized care and consolidation of rural hospitals, safe and efficient care transitions via interhospital transfers, particularly for patients in the emergency department (ED), are of paramount importance to ensure optimal patient outcomes. Transferred patients are at higher risk for mortality, longer hospital stays, and increased costs.

pmc-12564015.title: Comparative Chemical and Physical Characterization of Biomimetic Versus Commercial Hydroxyapatites for Tooth Enamel Repair
pmc-12564015.creator: Marco Lelli, Ismaela Foltran, Rossella Pucci, Fabrizio Tarterini, Hermann Ehrlich
pmc-12564015.description: Background: Substituted hydroxyapatites (HAps) are widely used in oral-care formulations for enamel repair; however, head-to-head comparisons among commercial grades remain limited. Objective: To compare four commercial HAps: A (Kal-HAp), B (FL-HAp), C (FL-HAp-SC), and D (microRepair®, a biomimetic Zn–carbonate-substituted HAp) and to evaluate their ability to form an enamel-like coating in vitro.

pmc-12677964.title: Characterisation and Phylogenetic Analysis of the Complete Plastid Genome of Physalis minima L. from Malaysia
pmc-12677964.creator: Wei Lun Ng, Rebecca Jiayiin Ng, Douglas Law, Qiuying Ren, Charles Gnanaraj, Yoong Soon Yong, Shiou Yih Lee
pmc-12677964.description: Physalis minima L. is an herbaceous plant with ethnobotanic importance across many Asian cultures. In this study, we sequenced and assembled the plastid genome (plastome) of a P. minima sample from Malaysia, and conducted intraspecific pairwise and phylogenetic analyses with available data of its relatives.

pmc-12805259.description: ntext. •The case followed a classical clinical course of the improvement in conduction abnormalities, in response to antibiotics, in Lyme myocarditis. pmc-13379270.title: Body Image Concerns and Associated Factors up to Five Years After Cancer in Young Adulthood: A Swedish Longitudinal Population‐Based Study
pmc-13379270.creator: Rebecca Skog, Sarah Marklund, Claudia Lampic, Lena Wettergren
pmc-13379270.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate prevalence of body image disturbance and how perceptions of the body evolve from 1.5 to 5 years following a cancer diagnosis in young adulthood. Additionally, to identify factors associated with worse body image over time.
